about.title: about
about.body:
I am an artist, a daughter, a professional outlier, a teacher, a language shapeshifter, a player of archives, protocols, bureaucratic fictions, using crisis as muscle, impatience as rhythm, belonging as rumor, AI as mirror, through natural languages, legal tongue, poetry, code, dictionaries, precedents, interfaces, intimacy, film, Laurie Anderson, Adam Curtis, Nawal El Saadawi, Elinor Ostrom, the Code civil.

My work explores how language and technology create an uncanny sense of place, and how multitude helps us belong. In 2026, I co-founded KarmaLab, a creative studio focused on the thoughtful use of new media and emerging technology in the arts.

My films have screened on ARTE, France Télévisions, and Canal+, at Forum des Images, les FRAC, and Commune Image, as well as at festivals including Clermont-Ferrand, Go Short, L'Étrange Festival and Interfilm Berlin.

My teaching covers Systems Theory at Sciences Po, and formerly writing, translation, and digital media at LISAA Paris, INALCO, Concordia University, and Université Paul Valéry Montpellier III. It is shaped by my experience writing language manuals for Larousse Editions and translating poetry and prose.

IGLOÙ Paris, which I co-founded as a playground for experimental site-specific projects, created works merging digital formats with public space. One of these projects was presented at the 2018 Venice Architecture Biennale. The City of Paris later awarded us its Medal of Honor for contributions to its cultural landscape.

academia.title: academia
academia.body:
Research Interests

Sociolinguistics, critical pedagogy, migration studies, anthropology of belonging, affective computing, participatory arts, artistic practice in situations of crisis, systems theory, and cognitive neuroscience.

Currently, my research examines the concept of crisis through both linguistic and cultural lenses. I approach crises similarly to learning a new language as an adult, as well as technological shifts, investigating their impacts on human expression and behavior.


Teaching

2026-present Sciences Po - Lecturer in Systems Theory and Critical AI

ai.title: ai
ai.body:
Some people know me for my “AI-related activities”, which sounds vaguely criminal and is therefore staying. So I consolidated the evidence on one page.

What started as technical curiosity became a fairly elaborate relationship with consequences. Understanding hegemonic tools is the only way I know how to critique them, especially when you’re not their imagined default user.

I’m interested in synthetic images once they become convincing enough to pass as real, and in what that does to perception and authority. I use generative systems to make their construction visible rather than help them disappear.

Technically, as with every language I master, I approach AI as a grammar of fabrication. I build bespoke pipelines from crossbred models and stitched APIs. I started with ComfyUI in 2022, so most of what I use now has become idiosyncratic through practice.

Through KarmaLab, a studio I co-founded in 2026, I design hybrid pipelines across film, CGI, code, and generative systems, with transparency and environmental cost treated as part of production.

We also build public tools, among them a bias layer designed to make generative systems a little less eager to reproduce the same old world.

I spoke about this in an interview for ARTE, it’s in French though.

For the English speaking, I also made two parodies, Moustache and Women in AI, in response to two rather problematic AI contests, pushing their gender politics and generative biases until the machinery showed.

And that’s probably why I’m one of the Top 50 women AI filmmakers, recognized by Forbes.

>> I’m spending a lot of time speaking in rooms about these questions these days, in English and French. Some of those rooms are free to enter, so check Upcoming and come say hi.
